title: Implement Stack using Queues
spaceBreakdown:
- queue<int> q: up to n elements → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input, returned output
approach: Use a single queue. On `push(x)`, append `x` to the back, then rotate the queue `size−1` times (pop front, push back) so that `x` moves to the front. This makes the most recently pushed element the front of the queue, so `pop` and `top` are O(1) by simply accessing the front. `empty` delegates to the queue's empty check.
hints: A queue only lets you add to the back and remove from the front. After you insert a new element at the back, what would you do to the elements already ahead of it so that the new one comes out first?
Use a single queue. On `push(2)` when the queue is `[1]`, append 2 to get `[1, 2]`, then move the front element to the back once → `[2, 1]`. Now the front is the newest element.

```
push(x):
    q.push(x)
    sz = q.size()
    repeat sz - 1 times:
        q.push(q.front())
        q.pop()

pop():
    val = q.front()
    q.pop()
    return val

top():
    return q.front()

empty():
    return q is empty
```

**Two elements** - rotation count must be size−1, not size
`Input: ["MyStack","push","push","top"], [[],[1],[2],[]]` → `Expected: [null,null,null,2]`
⚠️ Bug: looping `q.size()` times instead of `q.size()-1` → after push(2), queue `[1,2]` rotated twice returns to `[1,2]`, top returns 1 instead of 2

**Push after pop** - queue state must stay correct across mixed operations
`Input: ["MyStack","push","push","pop","push","top"], [[],[1],[2],[],[3],[]]` → `Expected: [null,null,null,2,null,3]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping rotation on push (just appending) → after push(3) queue is `[1,3]`, top returns 1 instead of 3

**Empty after all pops** - empty check must reflect actual queue state
`Input: ["MyStack","push","pop","empty"], [[],[1],[],[]]` → `Expected: [null,null,1,true]`
⚠️ Bug: tracking emptiness with a separate boolean flag that isn't updated in pop → empty returns false

**Single element** - rotation on a one-element queue is a no-op, must still work
`Input: ["MyStack","push","top","pop","empty"], [[],[5],[],[],[]]` → `Expected: [null,null,5,5,true]`
⚠️ Bug: special-casing `size <= 1` and skipping push entirely → top returns garbage/uninitialized value

followUps.q: How would you implement this with exactly two queues, and what changes in complexity?
followUps.a: Use one main queue and one helper. On push, add to the helper, transfer all elements from main to helper, then swap the two. Push is O(n), pop/top/empty are O(1). Alternatively, push O(1) and pop O(n) by transferring n−1 elements to the helper on each pop.

followUps.q: What if push must be O(1) - can you still achieve it, and at what cost?
followUps.a: Yes - just append to the queue on push with no rotation (O(1)). But pop and top become O(n) because you must rotate n−1 elements to bring the last-added element to the front before accessing it. This trades push cost for pop/top cost.

followUps.q: How would you add a `size()` method, and does it affect complexity?
followUps.a: Return `q.size()` directly - O(1) time, O(1) space. The queue already tracks its element count internally, so no additional bookkeeping is needed.
